intro_train.title: The 10:47 PM Train
intro_train.narrator: Some notifications arrive at the wrong moment. Or maybe the right one.
intro_train.text:
The train is almost full.

Tired faces.
Wet coats.
Earbuds screwed into ears.

Outside, the rain turns the windows into trembling mirrors.

You look at your reflection without really seeing it.

The speaker announces your stop in a voice that is too gentle.

Then your phone buzzes.

A message.

Just one.

But your stomach tightens before you even open it.

ignorer_message.title: Don't Read It
ignorer_message.narrator: You can push a message away. Not always what it contains.
ignorer_message.text:
You set the phone face down on your leg.

For three seconds, you try to be someone who doesn't look.

You two had told yourselves it was over.
That it was better this way.

Then it vibrates again.

Same sender.

Same silence around you.

Your stop is approaching.

You know you should get up.

But your thumb has already woken the screen.

le_message.title: The Message
le_message.narrator: You didn't think a simple message could turn you around this much.
le_message.text:
The message is short.

> Before I leave, I wanted to tell you…

You read the sentence again.

Once.

Twice.

You two broke up three weeks ago.
Or maybe you were the one who left.
You no longer really know who decided.

The world around you grows blurrier.

You don't know what to feel: anger, sadness, relief, panic.

The train slows down.

The doors open.

A voice announces a station.

Not yours.

You look up with a jolt.

Your stop has gone by.

train_rate.title: Too Late
train_rate.narrator: Missing a stop is sometimes a dress rehearsal.
train_rate.text:
The doors begin to close.

You don't move.

Then your body decides for you.

You stand up too fast.

Someone grumbles.

Your bag bumps into a seat.

The chime of the doors speeds up your heartbeat.

You slip through at the last moment.

descente_precipitee.title: The Platform
descente_precipitee.narrator: Some seconds hold the full weight of a life.
descente_precipitee.text:
You get off too fast.

The platform is wet.

The crowd pushes you in every direction.

Your phone almost slips from your hand.

You want to catch it.

Someone bumps into you.

Your foot searches for the edge.

It doesn't find it.

A cry.

A metallic sound.

A light.

Then nothing.

sur_les_rails.title: Still on the Tracks
sur_les_rails.narrator: The silence after a fall never sounds like the silence before.
sur_les_rails.text:
You open your eyes.

You are still on the tracks.

But the station is no longer the same.

No train.
No crowd.
No cries.

Cold neon lights the platform.
You hear rain in the distance.

You sit up slowly.

On every sign, the same time:

**10:47 PM**

Platform 1. Platform 4. Platform 18. Platform 52.

Always:

**10:47 PM**

A gray cat crosses the tracks in front of you.

It stops.

Looks at you.

Then calmly climbs onto the platform.

appel_gare.title: No One Answers
appel_gare.narrator: In some places, shouting mostly serves to hear your own fear.
appel_gare.text:
You call out.

Your voice gets lost beneath the glass roof.

No one answers.

Then the speaker crackles:

> Travelers who arrived by accident are asked to head to their inner platform.

You don't understand.

The cat meows.

Or maybe the sound comes from the speakers.

premier_quai.title: Station of Regrets
premier_quai.narrator: All trains leave at the same time. Every one promises a different direction.
premier_quai.text:
The central hall is immense.

Lines stretch out as far as you can see.

Every sign shows:

**Departure: 10:47 PM**

But the destinations resemble no city.

Line 03 — The Life That Stayed
Line 11 — The Successful Life
Line 18 — The Childhood That Stayed
Line 27 — The Empty Platform
Line 34 — The Train of the Exhausted
Line 52 — The Accelerated Life
Line 74 — Messages Never Sent

A woman sitting on a bench looks up at you.

**"First time?"**

voyageuse.title: The Soaked Traveler
voyageuse.narrator: Some have been waiting so long they've forgotten what they were hoping for.
voyageuse.text:
The woman looks at the signs.

**"Here, everyone is looking for the right train."**

You ask where they're going.

She laughs softly.

**"Somewhere we could have been happy. That's what we believe at first."**

She shows you your phone.

The screen is black.

Then it turns on by itself.

The message is still there.

But one line has changed:

> I think we should have chosen each other sooner.
> Or maybe learned to choose ourselves.

The woman murmurs:

**"The station likes to correct sentences."**

comment_partir.title: How to Leave
comment_partir.narrator: The simplest question is often the one that scares the most.
comment_partir.text:
**"How do I get out of here?"**

The traveler shrugs.

**"You can always get on a train. The problem is knowing whether you really want to get off."**

She looks at the cat.

**"Some people stay in one life. Others keep coming back here again and again. Others wait for the last departure."**

**"And you?"**

She smiles.

**"Me? I'm waiting to stop waiting."**

hub_gare.title: The Lines of 10:47 PM
hub_gare.narrator: Every destination looks like an answer. None of them really is one.
hub_gare.text:
The signs change slowly.

The same lines come back.

The cat sits in front of you as if it had been waiting for you.

On your phone, the message stays open.

There's no signal anymore.

Yet the time still reads:

**10:47 PM**

hub_gare_2.title: The Other Lines
hub_gare_2.narrator: The more you explore, the more the destinations seem to know you.
hub_gare_2.text:
The board turns with a mechanical noise.

New destinations appear.

Line 34 — The Train of the Exhausted
Line 52 — The Accelerated Life
Line 74 — Messages Never Sent

Everything leaves at 10:47 PM.

Always.

choices.text: Line 34 — The Train of the Exhausted

retour_gare.title: Back to 10:47 PM
retour_gare.text:
The train slows down.

The doors open.

You get off.

The central hall is there.

Exactly as you left it.

The cat is asleep on an information board.

The time hasn't moved.

**10:47 PM**

telephone_change.title: The Phone
telephone_change.text:
Your phone lights up.

The message has been completed.

There was more.

> Before I leave, I wanted to tell you…
> that it had nothing to do with you.
> That maybe I needed to disappear a little.
> Not from you. Just from myself.
> I don't know if you understand.

You read the words one by one.

*Disappear a little.*

What that meant.
What it may still mean.

You don't know.

You may never know whether it was an ending
or just a pause.

The cat opens one eye.

Then the line board crackles.

ligne_03_intro.title: Line 03 — The Life That Stayed
ligne_03_intro.narrator: Some trains don't head somewhere new, but toward the place you never left.
ligne_03_intro.text:
Train 03 smells of dust and old heating.

Through the window, you see your hometown.

Younger.
Quieter.
More golden.

The voice announces:

> Next stop: the life you would have had by staying.

vie_restee_1.title: Hometown
vie_restee_1.narrator: There are towns you can't leave. Or never really bother to leave.
vie_restee_1.text:
The main street has barely changed.

The bakery is still open.
The old cinema is showing films you had forgotten.
Someone calls your name from a café terrace.

You once had a chance to leave.
A long time ago.
A job in another city.
An acceptance letter you never sent.

You told yourself: *next time*.

There was no next time.

And it's not a tragedy.
It's just what happened.

choices.text: Go to the café with old friends

vie_restee_2.title: Like Every Thursday
vie_restee_2.narrator: Habits can look a lot like love. Or like a very comfortable cage.
vie_restee_2.text:
The coffee is hot.

The conversation is easy.

You talk about the weather, the neighbors, the roadworks on the square, the people who've left.

When someone mentions those who left, there's a one-second silence.
No one comments.
Everyone noticed.

You look at your cup.

You could have been one of those people they talk about in that silence.

vie_restee_seule.title: Streets Too Familiar
vie_restee_seule.narrator: You can lose yourself in a place you know too well.
vie_restee_seule.text:
You walk alone.

At every corner, a memory.

The first lie.
The first shame.
The first urge to leave.

This town didn't destroy you.

It kept you.

That's different.

On the platform of the small station, a train passes without stopping.

You don't know whether you regret it or envy it.

choices.text: Return to the Station of Regrets

fin_vie_restee.title: Ending — The Life That Stayed
fin_vie_restee.text:
You stay.

Time keeps passing.

The Thursday coffees go on.
The streets keep their names.
The faces age at a reasonable pace.

One evening, you find the acceptance letter again.
Never sent.
The ink is still readable.

You put it in a drawer.

Not to remember it.
To stop searching for it.

ligne_11_intro.title: Line 11 — The Successful Life
ligne_11_intro.narrator: Some trains sell you lights before they mention the price.
ligne_11_intro.text:
Train 11 is modern, shiny, almost silent.

In the window, your reflection changes.

Better clothes.
A more confident gaze.
A phone full of notifications.

The voice announces:

> Next stop: the life where you succeeded.

reussie_1.title: The Spotlight
reussie_1.narrator: There is a version of you who said yes to everything they were asked.
reussie_1.text:
You hear your name chanted by an immense crowd.

Someone is doing your makeup.
Someone is adjusting your jacket.
Someone tells you you're late.

After a few seconds, you understand that this is your life.

That you wanted it.
That for it, you canceled a dinner one night.
Then two.
Then an entire relationship.

That person had said: *I can't keep waiting around for your career.*

You had replied: *I understand.*

You had lied.

reussie_2.title: The Crowd
reussie_2.narrator: A crowd can fill a hall and still leave someone alone in the middle of it.
reussie_2.text:
The audience is screaming.

You know the songs almost by reflex.

Your body plays the role to perfection.

When the song ends, the applause washes over you without really reaching you.

Later, in the dressing room, strangers congratulate you.

They know your name.

Not your silences.

reussie_loges.title: The Silent Dressing Room
reussie_loges.narrator: The room is full of gifts and flowers. Yet it feels empty.
reussie_loges.text:
You lock yourself in the dressing room.

The walls are covered in flowers.
Cards.
Trophies.

On a table, a phone shows hundreds of messages.

You search for one name in particular.

It isn't there.

It hasn't sent a message in three years.
Not since that dinner you canceled one last time.

fin_vie_reussie.title: Ending — The Successful Life
fin_vie_reussie.narrator: Success is a kind of loneliness no one pities.
fin_vie_reussie.text:
You stay.

The halls fill up.
The lights come on.
People sing your name.

You learn to smile at the right moment.
To reply quickly.
To thank people sincerely.

Some nights, you search the audience for a face you recognize.

Not a fan.
Someone.

They're never there.

But people applaud.
And that's something.

ligne_18_intro.title: Line 18 — The Childhood That Stayed
ligne_18_intro.narrator: You never really go back to childhood. You only visit the memory you kept of it.
ligne_18_intro.text:
Train 18 has seats that are too small.

The windows are decorated with stickers.
An old school bag sits by the door.

The voice announces:

> Next stop: the time when dreams were not yet ashamed.

enfance_1.title: The Bedroom
enfance_1.narrator: Somewhere there is a version of you who never stopped drawing.
enfance_1.text:
You are in your childhood bedroom.

The walls are lower.
The colors brighter.
The toys exactly where they belong.

But you are an adult.

In the mirror, you have today's face.
In the room, you have your earlier hands.

There's a date in a notebook.
The year you stopped.

Not because of a failure.
Not because of a criticism.

You were afraid it wouldn't be enough.
So you chose something that was enough for sure.

It was a reasonable decision.

choices.text: Look at the drawing of the station

enfance_2.title: The Little Version
enfance_2.narrator: Children ask the questions we spend our lives avoiding.
enfance_2.text:
The child looks at you seriously.

**"Why did you stop?"**

You ask what she means.

She shows you drawings.
Notebooks.
Ideas for impossible worlds you meant to explore.

You could answer: *I was scared*.
Or: *I needed a steady paycheck*.
Or: *nobody encouraged me at the right time*.

All three are true.
None is enough.

choices.text: Promise her you won't forget again

enfance_dessin.title: The Drawing
enfance_dessin.narrator: Some things were there before we understood them.
enfance_dessin.text:
The drawing shows a huge station.

All the trains display the same time.

**10:47 PM**

You ask the child how she imagined it.

She shrugs.

**"I didn't imagine it. I remember it."**

The gray cat is drawn in a corner of the page.

choices.text: Return to the station with the drawing in mind

fin_enfance.title: Ending — The Childhood That Stayed
fin_enfance.narrator: Some lives we abandon go on without us.
fin_enfance.text:
You stay.

The days become simple.

Drawings.
Snacks.
Rain against the windows.
Stories before bed.

No one asks you to succeed.
No one counts your failures.

But sometimes, at night, you wonder what those impossible worlds would have become.

If someone had drawn them all the way through.

ligne_27_intro.title: Line 27 — The Empty Platform
ligne_27_intro.narrator: Some destinations promise nothing. That's what makes them tempting.
ligne_27_intro.text:
Train 27 has no passengers.

Not even a driver.

The doors open without a sound.

The voice announces:

> Next stop: the place where no one can ask you for anything anymore.

vide_1.title: The Empty City
vide_1.narrator: Some people mistake silence for freedom.
vide_1.text:
The city looks normal.

Except there's no one in it.

No cars.
No voices.
No birds.

The shops are open.
The traffic lights work.

You once wanted this.
During a hard time.
You thought: *if only everyone would disappear*.

You were ashamed of that thought right away.

But it came back.
Several times.

vide_2.title: Asking Nothing
vide_2.narrator: Being alone is gentle when you know you could stop being alone.
vide_2.text:
You sit down in a park.

The wind moves the trees.
A fountain runs.
The world asks nothing of you.

You could stay here.

No disappointment.
No misunderstanding.
No expectations.

But you start looking for someone to show the fountain to.

And you understand something you already knew.

Silence is only pleasant when someone could break it.

vide_silhouette.title: The Silhouette
vide_silhouette.narrator: In empty worlds, we always end up looking for ourselves.
vide_silhouette.text:
At the far end of the avenue, someone is walking.

You run.

The silhouette speeds up without ever turning around.

The closer you get, the more it looks like you.

Then it disappears into a metro entrance.

On the sign:

**Departure: 10:47 PM**

fin_vide.title: Ending — The Empty Platform
fin_vide.narrator: You can choose absence. You don't choose what it takes with it.
fin_vide.text:
You stay.

The days no longer really have names.

You eat when you want.
You sleep when you want.
Sometimes you shout just to hear something.

One morning, you realize you've forgotten how to begin a sentence with someone else.

Not for lack of words.

For lack of practice.

ligne_34_intro.title: Line 34 — The Train of the Exhausted
ligne_34_intro.narrator: Some trains don't run on rails, but on exhaustion.
ligne_34_intro.text:
The train is packed. But no one talks.

No one talks.

Everyone is working: on a laptop, on a phone, inside their head.

Identical dark circles.
Rumpled suits.
Automatic smiles.

The voice announces:

> Next stop: the life where you never slowed down.

fatigues_1.title: The City That Never Sleeps
fatigues_1.narrator: Some people have learned to confuse exhaustion with worth.
fatigues_1.text:
The city glows all night.

The offices are full.
The cafés serve black drinks in nameless cups.
People walk fast, even those with nowhere to go.

At first, you told yourself: *it's temporary*.

That's what everyone says.
It's what everyone still believes years later.

You remember an evening when you could have said no.
One project too many.
One impossible favor.

You said yes because saying no felt like a form of weakness.

That evening, someone was waiting for you to have dinner.

fatigues_2.title: Already Late for Tomorrow
fatigues_2.narrator: When everything is urgent, nothing really is.
fatigues_2.text:
The floors all look alike.

Meetings.
Messages.
Targets.
Charts.

No one is shouting.

That's worse.

Everyone smiles as if exhaustion were proof of commitment.

You forgot a close friend's birthday.
You missed your mother's birthday once.
You missed something small and irreplaceable.

You no longer remember exactly what.

Maybe that's the most terrible part.

fatigues_refus.title: Stopping
fatigues_refus.narrator: In a running crowd, stopping feels like rebellion.
fatigues_refus.text:
You stop.

People walk around you without seeing you.

A man bumps into you.

**"Not now."**

You can't tell whether he's talking to you or to his own life.

The gray cat appears on a ticket machine.

It yawns.

Behind it, an escalator goes down toward a station where every clock reads 10:47 PM.

choices.text: Follow the cat to the station

fin_fatigues.title: Ending — The Train of the Exhausted
fin_fatigues.narrator: You end up looking like the hours you spend.
fin_fatigues.text:
You stay.

The years turn into weeks.
The weeks turn into lists.
The lists become the way you breathe.

You earn money.
You get things done.

One evening you find an old photo.
You look at yourself in it.

You wonder when you stopped looking like that person.

Not because of one event.
Because of all the little yeses.

ligne_52_intro.title: Line 52 — The Accelerated Life
ligne_52_intro.narrator: Some trains don't go anywhere. They just go too fast.
ligne_52_intro.text:
Train 52 shakes before it even leaves.

The announcements are rapid.
The doors slam.
The landscape is already rushing past while you're still on the platform.

The voice announces:

> Next stop: the life where you never wasted a minute.

acceleree_1.title: Everything Moves Faster
acceleree_1.narrator: Some people have learned to love speed so they never have to stop.
acceleree_1.text:
People talk too fast.

Coffee is served before it's ordered.
Children grow up between two red lights.
The seasons change while you're looking at your phone.

You once met someone who did everything slowly.
Who took the time to finish their sentences.
Who ordered a coffee and let it cool.

You found it strange.

Then annoying.

Then you understood, too late, that it was a way of being present.

You had already moved on to something else.

acceleree_2.title: Life, Optimized
acceleree_2.narrator: Every minute saved seems to demand a whole hour later on.
acceleree_2.text:
You learn to reply faster.
To eat faster.
To choose faster.
To forget faster.

The years pass in fragments.

A birthday.
A move.
A breakup.
A new start.

Everything goes so fast that nothing has time to leave a mark.

One morning, you can't remember which city you spent last Christmas in.

That isn't freedom.
It's wear and tear.

acceleree_lenteur.title: A Full Minute
acceleree_lenteur.narrator: Slowing down can be scarier than running.
acceleree_lenteur.text:
You sit on a bench.

No one understands.

Passersby look at you as if you had stopped breathing.

One minute passes.

A real one.

Long.

Imperfect.

You almost feel your heart take on a human rhythm again.

Then the cat jumps up beside you.

fin_acceleree.title: Ending — The Accelerated Life
fin_acceleree.narrator: Some lives look like a beautiful race toward nowhere.
fin_acceleree.text:
You stay.

Everything keeps moving.

You succeed quickly.
You change quickly.
You learn quickly.
You lose quickly.

One morning, looking at your reflection in a metro window, you can't remember the first name of your neighbor from your old apartment.

Nor the address.
Nor the neighborhood.

You still have destinations.
You barely have places left.

ligne_74_intro.title: Line 74 — Messages Never Sent
ligne_74_intro.narrator: Some trains carry the sentences that never found a recipient.
ligne_74_intro.text:
Train 74 is silent.

On the seats, switched-off phones.
Sealed envelopes.
Nameless notebooks.

The voice announces:

> Next stop: words kept too long.

messages_1.title: City of Messages
messages_1.narrator: The things we never said keep existing somewhere.
messages_1.text:
The streets are covered in messages.

Texts never sent.
Crumpled letters.
Voice notes hanging in the air like bubbles.

Some messages are tender.
Some are apologies.
Some are declarations that arrived too late.

You search for yours.

You find one you started one evening, at the station.
To someone who might still have been there.

You deleted it.

You told yourself it was too late.
That it wouldn't change anything.

That it was better to say nothing.

choices.text: Look for the message that brought you here

messages_2.title: The Original Message
messages_2.narrator: A sentence can change depending on who carries it.
messages_2.text:
You find the message.

It floats above a black fountain.

> I think we should have chosen each other sooner.

Then the sentence unfolds.

Versions of this message.
The one you wanted to send.
The one you were afraid to send.
The one that might have changed something.

Or nothing at all.

You will never know.

That's the real weight of this message.
Not what it says.
What it keeps you from knowing.

choices.text: Stay in this world of sentences

messages_autres.title: Other People's Words
messages_autres.narrator: You think you're alone with your regrets until you read other people's.
messages_autres.text:
You read.

Thousands of lives suspended in tiny sentences.

> I'm proud of you.
> Come back.
> I'm not angry anymore.
> I should have called.
> I never knew how to say I love you.

You cry without noticing.

Not only for yourself.

For everything people keep in their throats, hoping they'll still have tomorrow.

messages_repondre.title: Replying
messages_repondre.narrator: Some replies were never meant to be sent.
messages_repondre.text:
You write.

Not for the other person.

Not really.

You write for the person you were on the train.

For the one who lowered her eyes at the wrong moment.

> Maybe.
> But I'm tired of living the lives I didn't choose.

The message disappears.

Somewhere, a train arrives.

fin_messages.title: Ending — Messages Never Sent
fin_messages.narrator: Keeping other people's words is a way of not letting them disappear.
fin_messages.text:
You stay.

You read everything.

The apologies.
The confessions.
The tenderness that came too late.

You become the keeper of the sentences other people couldn't send.

Sometimes someone walks into the street looking for their message.
You show them where it is.

They cry or they laugh.
Rarely both at once.

You keep yours for last.

For the day you'll know what to do with it.

ligne_chat_verrouillee.title: The Gray Cat
ligne_chat_verrouillee.narrator: Some guides don't follow you at the beginning.
ligne_chat_verrouillee.text:
You follow the cat.

It crosses the hall.

Passes the lines.
Passes the travelers.
Passes the signs.

Then it stops in front of a platform with no number.

A black sign reads only:

**Line 88**

The cat looks at you.

Then the sign goes out.

Not yet.

ligne_88_intro.title: Line 88 — The Cat
ligne_88_intro.narrator: There is always a line that appears on no map.
ligne_88_intro.text:
The cat walks to the end of a platform you had never seen.

No train.

Just the tracks, the mist, and a clock stopped at 10:47 PM.

Then the cat jumps onto the tracks.

You want to shout.

But it doesn't fall.

It walks on the void.

Beneath its paws, images appear:
the hometown, the stage, the childhood bedroom, the empty city, the offices, the messages.

All the lines.
All the lives.
All the absences.

coeur_gare.title: The Heart of the Station
coeur_gare.narrator: This place may not be here to answer. Perhaps only to show.
coeur_gare.text:
You move on behind the cat.

The rails become a corridor of images.

You see yourself in every life.

The one who stayed.
The one who succeeded.
The one who never grew up.
The one who chose silence.
The one who ran too fast.
The one who lived among messages.

None is false.

None is perfect.

The cat stops in front of a train door with no destination.

On the door:

**Last departure — 10:47 PM**

choices.text: Go back and explore some more

dernier_depart.title: The Last Departure
dernier_depart.narrator: One day you have to choose without knowing what lies on the other side.
dernier_depart.text:
The final platform is empty.

No destination.
No line sign.

Only a clock.

**10:47 PM**

The train arrives without a sound.

Its windows glow with a warm light.

Almost real.

The cat sits in front of the doors.

The soaked traveler appears on the other side of the platform.

**"You can stay in one life. You can keep searching. Or you can get on."**

You ask where this train goes.

She smiles.

**"Nobody comes back with a clear answer."**

choices.text: Go back to explore the lines

final_train.title: The Train With No Destination
final_train.narrator: Some doors open onto an answer. Others onto a gentler question.
final_train.text:
You get on.

The doors close.

The train starts.

For a moment there is only the sound of the rails.

Then other sounds appear.

Very far away.

A voice.
Maybe your name.

A steady beep.
Maybe a machine.

Rain against a window.
Maybe the station.

You look at your reflection.

For a second, you think you see your face, wounded.

Then the reflection goes back to normal.

The cat is sitting on the seat across from you.

It slowly blinks.

The train slows down.

choices.text: Wait for the doors to open

fin_ambigue.title: Ending — The Doors Open
fin_ambigue.narrator: Some endings don't say whether you come back. They only ask what you would do if you did.
fin_ambigue.text:
Someone says your name.

Or maybe you're imagining it.

The doors open.

White light enters the car.

You take a step.

In your hand, your phone vibrates one last time.

On the screen:

> It is 10:48 PM.

You look up.

And you step forward.

fin_gare.title: Ending — Staying at 10:47 PM
fin_gare.narrator: Not choosing is also a way of living, but the station doesn't call it that.
fin_gare.text:
You stay.

The trains keep leaving.

The soaked traveler disappears one day.
Then maybe returns under a different coat.

You learn the lines.
The announcements.
The new arrivals.

You explain to others that they can look for the right life.

You know now that it doesn't exist.

But you keep watching the signs.

Because as long as every train leaves at 10:47, no possibility is truly lost.

It's comforting.

It's a prison.

Both at once.
